records.rule_or_error: TS2345: Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'TicketComplexityTier'
records.notes: A mistyped tier string would have routed the ticket through the wrong budget table at runtime; caught before commit.
Reference to a variable removed earlier in the same edit; would have thrown ReferenceError at first invocation.
An un-awaited state write raced the caller's next read — the writer/reader race class this codebase repeatedly hardens against.
A guarding null-check was deleted during a refactor; the flagged access was a genuine crash-on-null path.
Pre-existing long function untouched by the diff; the rule fired on the whole file, not on anything the change introduced.
Unused import left behind in a test-fixture generator; dead but harmless — no consumer, no runtime path.

records.notes: Unused local in a branch slated for deletion in the immediate follow-up commit; no behavioral effect.
Intentional CLI diagnostic console.log in a bin/ script; the rule doesn't distinguish library code from CLI output.
One-line docstring correction; no code path touched.
New optional field added with a safe default and covered by an existing test; lint+tsc clean, no observed regression.
Private helper renamed with every call site updated in the same commit; lint+tsc clean.
New CLI flag parsed through the existing validated-integer helper; lint+tsc clean.
Guard used '||' where '&&' was intended, inverting the condition; both operators type-check identically, so tsc is silent, and no lint rule targets boolean-operator intent.
Off-by-one in an array-slice boundary; the expression is type-correct, so tsc passes, and no lint rule targets loop/slice bounds.
A minutes value was passed where seconds was expected; both are plain 'number', so tsc cannot distinguish the units.
A duplicated 'git add' staged a bystander path outside the ticket's scope; the diff is syntactically and structurally valid, so lint+tsc are both green.
